results.name: Band Seated Neutral Grip Shoulders Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under the bench, with your arms bent, hands at shoulder level, and palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Press the handles of the band upwards until your arms are fully extended above your head, keeping your palms facing each other.
Slowly lower your hands back to shoulder level, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under the bench to prevent slipping.
results.description: Band Seated Neutral Grip Shoulders Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Band Seated Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored under the bench, with your arms bent, hands at shoulder level, and palms facing forward.
Press the handles of the band upwards until your arms are fully extended above your head, keeping your palms facing forward.
Slowly lower your hands back to shoulder level, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the exercise slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce the risk of injury.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under the bench to prevent slipping.
results.description: Band Seated Shoulder Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Band Single Arm Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and place one end of the resistance band securely under your foot of the working side. Hold the other end of the band in your working hand at shoulder height, palm facing inward.
Press the band overhead by fully extending your arm, keeping your wrist straight and elbow slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the band back to the starting position, maintaining control.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Use a controlled motion to press and lower the band to maximize muscle activation.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the band up and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure the band is securely anchored under your foot to prevent slipping.
results.description: Band Single Arm Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends of a resistance band anchored at head height in front of you. Keep your arms extended straight forward just higher than shoulder height with palms facing down.
Pull the band towards your chin by bending your elbows out to the sides, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly return to the starting position, extending your arms back to shoulder height.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you pull the band towards your chin and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement to maximize rear delt engagement.
Adjust the band’s resistance by stepping on it closer to or farther from the anchor point.
results.description: Band Standing Rear Delt Row is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Band Y Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the ends of two crossed resistance bands anchored at a low point on a sturdy equipment. Start with your arms hanging in front of your torso, palms facing your hips.
Raise your arms upward and outward to form a "Y" shape until your arms are in line with your shoulders.
Slowly return to the starting position, controlling the resistance band as you lower your arms.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily, exhaling as you raise your arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Keep your elbows slightly bent to avoid joint strain and focus on lifting with your shoulders.
Use an appropriate resistance band that challenges you without compromising your form.
results.description: Band Y Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Back Wide Shrug
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands behind your back. Your palms should face away from your body with a wide grip.
Keep your shoulders back and chest up. Slowly lift your shoulders towards your ears in a shrugging motion.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement, holding the contraction for a moment.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid rotating your shoulders; lift them straight up and down to prevent strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them.
Keep your arms straight throughout the exercise to focus the movement on your shoulders.
results.description: Barbell Back Wide Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Behind the Back Push Press Single Arm Balance
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with one hand behind your back. Your hand should be slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, with the barbell resting on your upper back and shoulder.
Slightly bend your knees, preparing to use your legs to generate power.

Push through your heels and extend your knees and hips explosively, pressing the barbell overhead with one arm until your arm is fully extended. Keep the bar slightly behind your head at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position behind your shoulder with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Maintain balance by focusing on a fixed point in front of you and keeping your core engaged.
Exhale forcefully as you press the barbell overhead and inhale as you bring it back down.
Ensure a smooth and controlled descent to maintain proper form and prevent injury.
results.description: Barbell Behind the Back Push Press Single Arm Balance is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the balance category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Bent Over Reverse Raise (Skier)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell behind your glutes with both hands, palms facing backward. Bend your knees and hinge at your hips, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Lower your torso until it is parallel to the floor, letting the barbell hang down under your hamstrings with your arms extended.
Keeping your arms straight, lift the barbell backward in a reverse raise motion until both arms are parallel to the floor.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift the barbell and inhale as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that provides enough resistance to challenge your muscles without compromising form.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Bent Over Reverse Raise (Skier) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Barbell Decline Shrug
instructions: Position a decline bench at a 45-degree angle. Lie face down on the bench with your forefeet firmly on the floor. Have a barbell placed on the floor underneath the bench within reach.
Grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Shrug your shoulders towards your ears, lifting the barbell straight up.
Slowly lower the barbell to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on squeezing your trapezius muscles at the top of the movement.
Avoid using your arms to lift the weight; the movement should come from your shoulders.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid looking up or down excessively.
results.description: Barbell Decline Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (Inside Squat Cage)
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline and position it inside a squat cage. Sit on the bench with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and press your back firmly against the bench. Lift the barbell off the rack and hold it at shoulder level with your elbows bent and pointing down.
Press the barbell overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your wrists straight and elbows slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder level with control, maintaining tension in your shoulders. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and prevent lower back strain.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you press the barbell overhead and inhale as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Incline Shoulders Press (Inside Squat Cage) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Triceps, Upper Back.
